title_en: Thirty-Three Chapters: Definitions of the Passions of the Rational Soul
author: Evagrius Ponticus
occasion: A monastic handbook defining spiritual diseases and symbolic figures, to help readers diagnose the soul's disorders and recognize spiritual realities.
argument: Evagrius defines a series of spiritual diseases that afflict the rational soul, each as a disposition, weakness, ignorance, or movement hindering virtue and the knowledge of God. Some are states of the soul (ἕξις, ἀδυναμία, ἄγνοια), others are movements or conditions (ζέσις, νεῦσις, ἔκκλισις), and some involve active opposition to spiritual realities. He then presents symbolic animals and natural figures, some representing practitioners at different stages of spiritual progress (ant, gecko, lion cub, rooster, he-goat), some representing unclean nations (rock badgers), some representing souls in defective states (unruled locusts), and others representing unclean powers or false knowledge (leech, woman, earth, fire, water, mocking eye) or holy powers (ravens, eaglets). The work moves from diseases of the soul to symbolic types of persons and spiritual forces. Its purpose is diagnostic and ascetic: to name the disorders so they can be recognized and resisted.

outline.move: Defines eight spiritual diseases of the rational soul, from jaundice to leprosy, each as a disposition or movement hindering virtue and knowledge of God.

Continues defining spiritual diseases and defects, including ecstasy (reversion to vice after virtue), bruising (practicing virtue not for its own sake), mutilation of nose (inability to perceive Christ's fragrance), mutilation of ear (hardness toward spiritual teaching), freckle (falling from spiritual contemplation or false understanding), speech impediment (inability to give thanks in all circumstances), lameness (weakness in practicing virtue), and dropsy (irrational inclination where vice prevails when virtues are extinguished).

Defines symbolic animals and figures: the ant (practical person storing food in this age), rock badgers (unclean nations receiving the Savior's commands), unruled locusts (rational souls not moved by death, nourished by seeds), gecko (practical mind relying on virtues and dwelling in knowledge of heavenly powers), lion cub (passionless person who has ruled the beasts within), rooster (spiritual person filled with knowledge proclaiming day from the intelligible sun), and he-goat (practical man rightly guiding disorderly thoughts).

Defines further symbolic figures: leech (unclean nature sucking just blood from rational souls), Hades (ignorance of rational nature arising from deprivation of the contemplation of God), woman (folly inviting rational souls to impurity), earth (worst disposition gathered from impiety and transgression), fire (destructive vice of rational nature against God's virtues), water (false knowledge extinguishing true knowledge), mocking eye (unclean nature mocking God's knowledge and dishonoring wisdom in created things), ravens (holy powers destructive of evils), ravines (rational souls hollowed out by vice and ignorance), and eaglets (holy powers entrusted to cast down the unclean).

key_terms.sense: The rational soul, the human soul capable of reason and knowledge of God
A settled disposition or state of the soul, here always a bad one
Vice or wickedness, the opposite of virtue
Virtue, especially the practical virtues that form Christ in the soul
Knowledge of God, the goal of the spiritual life
Contemplation, especially of God and of created things
The practical virtues, the active virtues of the ascetic life
Ignorance, especially ignorance of God and spiritual realities
An unclean nature, a spiritual being or power opposed to God
Holy powers, angelic or heavenly beings that destroy vices
Spiritual teaching, the instruction that nourishes the soul
The mind or intellect, the highest part of the soul capable of contemplation
Freedom from the passions, the state of mastery over inner beasts

scripture: The work alludes to Levitical purity laws and biblical animal imagery but does not cite books by name. Where biblical references appear in translation, use standard modern English Bible book names and LXX Psalm numbering.
uncertain: The precise addressee is not stated in the text.
The exact date of composition is not given in the text; late 4th century is inferred from Evagrius's known period of activity.
Whether the symbolic animals in chapters 17-24 and 31-33 are drawn from specific biblical passages is not made explicit in the text.

_unresolved_facts.claim: mutilation of nose (inability to perceive Christ's fragrance)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Κολόβωσις ῥινός, ἔστι στέρησις ἀρετῆς ἀντιλαμβανομένης εὐωδίας τῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: mutilation of nose: deprivation of the virtue that perceives the fragrance of Christ

_unresolved_facts.claim: mutilation of ear (hardness toward spiritual teaching)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὠτότμησις. ἔστι σκληρία λογικῆς ψυχῆς πρὸς τὴν πνευματικὴν διδασκαλίαν ἀνθέλκουσα
_unresolved_facts.fix: mutilation of ear: hardness of the rational soul that draws back from spiritual teaching

_unresolved_facts.claim: freckle (falling from spiritual contemplation or false understanding)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐφηλὶς, ἔστι πνευματικῆς θεωρίας ἔκπτωσις, ἢ τῆς τῶν γεγονότων θεωρίας οὐκ ἀληθὴς κατανόησις
_unresolved_facts.fix: freckle: a falling away from spiritual contemplation, or a false understanding of the contemplation of created things

_unresolved_facts.claim: speech impediment (inability to give thanks in all circumstances)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Μογιλαλία, ἔστι πάθος τοῦ λογιστικοῦ μέρους τῆς ψυχῆς, καθ' ὃ σκανδαλιζόμενος ἐπὶ τοῖς γινομένοις ἐν παντὶ εὐχαριστεῖν ἀδυνατεῖ τῷ Θεῷ
_unresolved_facts.fix: speech impediment: a passion of the rational part of the soul, by which one, being scandalized at what happens, is unable to give thanks to God in all things

_unresolved_facts.claim: dropsy (irrational inclination where vice prevails when virtues are extinguished)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὕδρωψ, ἔστιν ἔκκλισις ἄλογος ψυχῆς, καθ' ἣν σβεσθεισῶν τῶν ἀρετῶν ἐπικρατεῖ κακία καὶ ἀγνωσία
_unresolved_facts.fix: dropsy: an irrational inclination of the soul, by which, when the virtues are extinguished, vice and ignorance prevail

_unresolved_facts.claim: unruled locusts (rational souls not moved by death, nourished by seeds)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἀβασίλευτοι ἀκρίδες, ψυχαὶ λογικαὶ μὴ σαλευόμεναι ὑπὸ τοῦ θανάτου καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν σπερμάτων διατρεφόμεναι
_unresolved_facts.fix: unruled locusts: rational souls not shaken by death and nourished by seeds

_unresolved_facts.claim: gecko (practical mind relying on virtues and dwelling in knowledge of heavenly powers)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἀσκαλαβότης, ἔστι νοῦς πρακτικὸς, ἐπερειδόμενος ἀρεταῖς καὶ κατοικῶν ἐν ταῖς γνώσεσι τῶν οὐρανίων δυνάμεων
_unresolved_facts.fix: gecko: a practical mind, leaning upon virtues and dwelling in the knowledges of heavenly powers

_unresolved_facts.claim: rooster (spiritual person filled with knowledge proclaiming day from the intelligible sun)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἀλεκτρυὼν, ἔστιν ἄνθρωπος πνευματικὸς πληρούμενος γνώσεως καὶ ἑτέραις εὐαγγελιζόμενος ψυχαῖς τὴν παρὰ τοῦ νοητοῦ ἡλίου γενομένην ἡμέραν
_unresolved_facts.fix: rooster: a spiritual person filled with knowledge and evangelizing to other souls the day that comes from the intelligible sun

_unresolved_facts.claim: he-goat (practical man rightly guiding disorderly thoughts)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Τράγος, ἔστιν ἀνὴρ πρακτικὸς τῶν ἐν αὐτῷ ἀτάκτων λογισμῶν ὀρθῶς καθηγούμενος
_unresolved_facts.fix: he-goat: a practical man rightly leading the disorderly thoughts within him

_unresolved_facts.claim: Hades (ignorance of rational nature arising from deprivation of the contemplation of God)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἅδης, ἔστιν ἄγνοια φύσεως λογικῆς κατὰ στέρησιν τοῦ Θεοῦ θεωρίας ἐπισυμβαίνουσα
_unresolved_facts.fix: Hades: ignorance of rational nature arising from deprivation of the contemplation of God

_unresolved_facts.claim: woman (folly inviting rational souls to impurity)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Γυνὴ, ἔστιν ἀφροσύνη λογικὰς ψυχὰς ἐπὶ ἀκαθαρσίαν προσκαλουμένη
_unresolved_facts.fix: woman: folly inviting rational souls to impurity

_unresolved_facts.claim: earth (worst disposition gathered from impiety and transgression)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Γῆ, ἔστιν ἕξις χειρίστη ἐξ ἀσεβείας καὶ παρανομίας συλλεγομένη
_unresolved_facts.fix: earth: worst disposition gathered from impiety and transgression

_unresolved_facts.claim: fire (destructive vice of rational nature against God's virtues)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Πῦρ, ἔστι κακία φύσεως λογικῆς φθαρτικὴ τῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀρετῶν
_unresolved_facts.fix: fire: vice of rational nature destructive of the virtues of God

_unresolved_facts.claim: water (false knowledge extinguishing true knowledge)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὕδωρ, ἔστι γνῶσις ψευδὴς σβεστικὴ γνώσεως ἀληθοῦς
_unresolved_facts.fix: water: false knowledge extinguishing true knowledge

_unresolved_facts.claim: mocking eye (unclean nature mocking God's knowledge and dishonoring wisdom in created things)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὀφθαλμὸς καταγελῶν, ἔστι φύσις ἀκάθαρτος τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ καταγελῶσα γνώσεως καὶ ἀτιμάζουσα τὴν ἐν τοῖς γεγονόσι σοφίαν
_unresolved_facts.fix: mocking eye: unclean nature mocking the knowledge of God and dishonoring the wisdom in created things

_unresolved_facts.claim: ravens (holy powers destructive of evils)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Κόρακες, εἰσὶ δυνάμεις ἅγιαι, φθαρτικαὶ τῶν κακιῶν
_unresolved_facts.fix: ravens: holy powers destructive of evils

_unresolved_facts.claim: ravines (rational souls hollowed out by vice and ignorance)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Φάραγγες, εἰσὶ ψυχαὶ λογικαὶ κοιλανθεῖσαι ἀπὸ κακίας καὶ ἀγνωσίας
_unresolved_facts.fix: ravines: rational souls hollowed out by vice and ignorance

_unresolved_facts.claim: eaglets (holy powers entrusted to cast down the unclean)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Νεοσσοὶ ἀετῶν, εἰσὶ δυνάμεις ἅγιαι τοὺς ἀκαθάρτους καταβάλλειν πεπιστευμέναι
_unresolved_facts.fix: eaglets: holy powers entrusted to cast down the unclean
